mainTopic: The guard posts of the כהנים and לוים, and the בית המוקד where the כהנים slept
overview: The גמרא goes through the משנה's description of the places where the כהנים kept guard at night. First it asks whether בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ were real upper stories or just tall rooms. A משנה in מסכת מדות shows there was a real upper story over שער הניצוץ, with the כהנים guarding above and the לוים below. A ברייתא on במדבר 18:2 explains why: the לוים join the כהנים in the כהנים' own job of guarding. Next, the משנה describes the בית המוקד as a large domed hall. The גמרא asks how one guard was enough when the room had two gates, and אביי answers that the gates were close enough for one guard to watch both. The room's stone ledges raise a question from the פסוק that the מקדש was built of whole stone, and אביי answers that the stones were prepared beforehand in small and large sizes. The elders slept on these ledges rather than on beds, since bringing beds into the מקדש is not respectful. The young כהנים slept on the floor, and the גמרא begins asking why they have a different name elsewhere, a question that finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the two chambers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the words of the משנה that named בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ as upper stories.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Chamber of Avtinas and the Chamber of the Spark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can ask a question about it. This step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said these two rooms were upper stories (עליות). The גמרא picks up those words because it wants to clarify exactly what 'upper story' means here.

keyTerms.meaning: The chamber of the אבטינס family, who prepared the קטורת (incense)
The Chamber of the Spark, one of the guard posts in the בית המקדש
An upper story; a room on a second floor

phrases.english: The Chamber of Avtinas and the Chamber of the Spark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה lists בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ as upper stories.

steps.title: Were they real upper stories or just tall rooms?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether these rooms were truly built on a second floor, or were only raised up high so they looked like upper stories.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Were they actual upper stories, or were they just very tall, so that they looked like upper stories?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'upper stories': a real second floor, or just a tall raised room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand עליות. Either a room was really built on top of another room, or the room stood up high, perhaps on pillars, and only looked like a second floor. The גמרא wants to know which is true.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised (an open question the Sages were unsure about)

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Were they actual upper stories,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא דַּהֲווֹ גְּבִיהִי מִגְבָּהּ כַּעֲלִיּוֹת?
phrases.english: or perhaps they were just very tall, like upper stories?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the משנה's term 'upper stories' means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the chambers were real upper floors or only tall raised rooms.

steps.title: A משנה shows there was a real upper story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת מדות that describes a real upper story built on top of שער הניצוץ, where the כהנים guarded above and the לוים below.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as we learned in a משנה: Of the gates in the north, the Gate of the Spark was like a portico, with an upper story built on top of it. The priests kept watch from above and the Levites from below. It also had an entrance to the non-sacred area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a משנה that says an upper story was built on top of שער הניצוץ. So it was a real second floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'an upper story built on top of it' show a room really sitting on top of another structure, not just a tall room. The משנה also tells us that the כהנים guarded up there and the לוים guarded below. This detail sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Gate of the Spark, on the north side of the עזרה
A portico: a roofed structure open on the sides
The non-sacred area, meaning the less holy area outside the עזרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the איבעיא. It also brings up the detail of כהנים above and לוים below, which the rest of the סוגיא will explain.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as we learned in a Mishnah:
Of the gates in the north, the Gate of the Spark
was like a kind of portico,
and an upper story was built on top of it,
so that the priests keep watch from above,
and the Levites from below.
And it had an entrance to the non-sacred area.
phrases.notes: It opened out onto the הר הבית, which is less holy than the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 from a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were real upper stories, since the משנה says a room was built on top of שער הניצוץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת מדות about the northern gates.

steps.title: Where do we learn the split between guards above and below?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the כהנים guard from above and the לוים from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the rule comes from that כהנים guard upstairs and לוים guard downstairs. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only described how the guarding was set up. Now the גמרא wants the source in the תורה that explains why the כהנים are on top and the לוים are below.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means: where do we learn that כהנים guard above and לוים guard below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a detail mentioned in the משנה of step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the כהנים guard from above and the לוים from below.

steps.title: The verse says the Levites join the priests' service
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'that they may join you and serve you' as saying the לוים join the כהנים in the כהנים' own job.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'That they may join you and serve you.' The verse is speaking about your service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains a פסוק. The פסוק means the לוים join the כהנים in the כהנים' own service, which is guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your service' means אהרן's service, so the לוים are added on to the כהנים' guarding. Because they only join the כהנים, the כהנים hold the main post above and the לוים guard below.

keyTerms.meaning: Your service (the service of אהרן and the כהנים)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"That they may join you and serve you"
The verse is speaking about your service.
phrases.notes: 'Your' means אהרן and the כהנים. The לוים join the כהנים' own job of guarding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by citing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר 18:2 teaches that the לוים accompany the כהנים in the כהנים' guarding.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the Levites' own service
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own reading: perhaps the פסוק is talking about the לוים's own jobs, not the כהנים' service.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say the verse is speaking about your service, or perhaps it is only about their service!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions itself. Maybe 'serve you' means the לוים's own special work, such as carrying the כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק were about the לוים's own work, it would not teach anything about the לוים joining the כהנים in guarding. Then we would have no source for guarding above and below.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only, perhaps it really means
You say... (opening of a self-challenge in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: You say the verse is speaking about your service,
or perhaps it is only about their service!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בַּעֲבוֹדָתְךָ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בַּעֲבוֹדָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'serve you' refers to the כהנים' service.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words could just as well describe the לוים's own work, so they would not prove anything about guarding.

steps.title: Another verse already covers the Levites' own service
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that a different פסוק already speaks about the לוים's own service, so this פסוק must be about the כהנים' service.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'And they shall join you and keep watch over all its vessels and all its service,' their own service is already stated. So how do I explain 'That they may join you and serve you'? The verse is speaking about your service.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its challenge. The לוים's own work is already written in another פסוק, so this פסוק must be teaching something else: the כהנים' service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not need to say the same thing twice. A later פסוק already covers the לוים guarding the כלים and the work. So the earlier פסוק must be about the לוים joining the כהנים in the כהנים' own guarding.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I fulfill (explain) this verse?

phrases.english: When it says
"And they shall join you and keep watch
over all its vessels and all its service"
their own service is already stated.
So how do I fulfill
"That they may join you and serve you"?
The verse is speaking about your service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and goes back to the reading of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Avoiding repetition: another פסוק already covers the other reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Serve you' might refer to the לוים's own work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since another פסוק already covers the לוים's own work, 'serve you' must refer to joining the כהנים' service.

steps.title: Priests guard above, Levites guard below
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes how this works in practice: the כהנים guard from above and the לוים from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Priests keep watch from above, and Levites from below.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the practical result. The כהנים guard on the upper level and the לוים on the lower level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוים join the כהנים' guarding as helpers, so the כהנים take the higher, main post. This is exactly the setup the משנה described at שער הניצוץ.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (how does this work in practice)

steps.whatToRemember: The rooms were real upper stories. The כהנים guarded upstairs and the לוים downstairs, because במדבר 18:2 teaches that the לוים join the כהנים in the כהנים' own guarding.

phrases.english: How so?
Priests keep watch from above,
and Levites from below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of the reading proven in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כהנים guard from above and לוים from below, which answers the question of step 4.

steps.title: The Chamber of the Hearth was a large domed hall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the בית המוקד had a dome-shaped ceiling and was a large hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Chamber of the Hearth had a domed ceiling, and it was a large hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which describes the בית המוקד, the third place where the כהנים kept guard. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4-8 explained why כהנים and לוים guard the מקדש. Now the משנה describes the room where the כהנים guarded and slept. The details here, a big room with stone rows around it, are what the גמרא examines next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Chamber of the Hearth, a heated room where the כהנים on duty guarded and slept

phrases.english: The Chamber of the Hearth was a dome,
and it was a large hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source for guarding (Steps 4-8) to the משנה's description of the בית המוקד guard post.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית המוקד was a large hall with a domed ceiling.

steps.title: Two gates, yet only one guard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how there could be only one guard post in the בית המוקד when another משנה says it had two gates, one of them with a small side door.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there really only one guard in the Chamber of the Hearth? A contradiction is raised: the Chamber of the Hearth had two gates. One opened to the חיל and one opened to the עזרה. רבי יהודה said: the gate that opened into the עזרה had a small door in it, which the כהנים used to go in and check the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of one guard in the בית המוקד. It quotes a משנה showing the room had two gates, so it seems two guards would be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guard count gives the בית המוקד only one guard. But if each gate needs watching, two gates should mean two guards. רבי יהודה's added detail about a small door makes the gate into the עזרה an active entrance that also needs watching.

keyTerms.meaning: The rampart, a strip of ground around the inner area of the מקדש
A small door set inside a larger gate
To search or check an area

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד שׁוֹמֵר הוּא דַּהֲוָה בְּבֵית הַמּוֹקֵד?
phrases.english: And was there only one guard in the Chamber of the Hearth?
And a contradiction is raised:
There were two gates in the Chamber of the Hearth,
one open to the rampart,
and one open to the courtyard.
Rabbi Yehuda said:
This one, through which they enter the courtyard,
had a small door,
through which they would enter to check the courtyard!

steps.triggerLanguage: וחד שומר הוא דהוה בבית המוקד? ורמינהי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number of guards in the room described in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of only one guard in the בית המוקד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says the room had two gates, each a real entrance, so it seems two guards would be needed.

steps.title: The gates were close enough for one guard
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the two gates stood near each other, so one guard could watch both.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: since the two gates stood next to each other, one guard was enough. He could look this way and look that way.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. Two gates do not need two guards when one person can see both from where he stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that every gate needs its own guard. אביי shows that this is not always so: what matters is whether the gates can be watched. Since they were close together, one guard covered both, and there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: The בית המוקד had two gates but one guard, because the gates were close enough for one person to watch both.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Since they stood next to each other,
one guard was enough for them,
he looks here and looks there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי: כיון דגבי הדדי הוו קיימי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification of where the gates stood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two gates would need two separate guards.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gates were close together, so one guard could watch both.

steps.title: The room was surrounded by rows of stone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: the בית המוקד was surrounded by rows of stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was surrounded by rows of stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה about the בית המוקד. This sets up the question of what these 'rows of stone' were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new detail about the room. The משנה uses an unusual word, רובדין, and the גמרא is about to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rows or layers of stone along the walls

phrases.english: Surrounded by rows of stone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's description of the בית המוקד (Step 9) for its next detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית המוקד was surrounded by rows of stone.

steps.title: What are these rows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word רובדין means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are these 'rows'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word רובדין in the משנה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about the meaning of a word, not a challenge. The גמרא wants to know what the stones looked like and what they were used for.

phrases.english: What are these rows?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word in Step 12 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word רובדין

steps.title: Stone steps leading up to a stone bench
steps.stepSummary: The רובדין were cut stone ledges that the כהנים used to climb up to a higher stone bench.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were cut stone ledges, which the כהנים climbed to reach a higher stone ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the 'rows' were stone ledges sticking out from the wall, arranged as steps up to a higher bench.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the room had stepped stone benches along the walls. The lower stones served as steps, and the higher ledge was where the כהנים could lie down. Calling them 'cut stones' (גזרתא) sets up the next question about splitting stones in the מקדש.

phrases.english: Cut stones of a bench,
by which they go up to a bench.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רובדין were cut stone ledges used to climb up to a higher bench.

steps.title: Were stones cut, if the Temple was built of whole stones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this explanation from the פסוק saying the בית המקדש was built of whole stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really split stones? But it is written: 'And the house, when it was being built, was of whole stone...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 14. Cut stone ledges seem to go against the פסוק that the בית המקדש was built of whole stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 called the ledges 'cut stones,' which suggests the builders split stones to make the steps. But the פסוק says the house was built of whole stone, which seems to rule out cutting stones in the building. So how could the room have these ledges?

phrases.english: And would they split stones?
But isn't it written: 'And the house, when it was being built, was of whole stone, etc.'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of רובדין in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the רובדין were cut stones
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the בית המקדש was built of whole stone, which seems to rule out cutting stones to make ledges.

steps.title: Small and large stones were prepared ahead of time
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the builders prepared the stones beforehand and brought both small and large ones, as the פסוק mentions stones of ten and of eight אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: they prepared the stones and brought small stones and large stones from the start, as it is written: 'stones of ten אמות and stones of eight אמות.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. Nothing was split at the building site. The stones arrived already prepared, in different sizes, and the different sizes made the ledges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that ledges mean cutting stones in the building. אביי says the stones were finished beforehand and came in small and large sizes, so placing them created ledges along the wall. A second פסוק proves that stones of different sizes were used.
steps.whatToRemember: The stone ledges in the בית המוקד did not go against the rule of 'whole stone.' The stones were prepared ahead of time in small and large sizes, and the different sizes formed the ledges.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא fits a physical detail of the מקדש together with a פסוק about how the מקדש was built.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They would prepare and bring from the start
phrases.notes: He means the stones were made ready before they came, so nothing was split at the building.

phrases.english: small stones and large stones,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדִכְתִיב: ״אַבְנֵי עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת וְאַבְנֵי שְׁמֹנֶה אַמּוֹת״.
phrases.english: as it is written: 'stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי: דמתקני ומייתי מעיקרא אבני זוטרתא ואבני רברבתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification of how the stones were prepared, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stone ledges would mean splitting stones in the building, against 'whole stone.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The stones were prepared beforehand in small and large sizes, and the different sizes formed the ledges.

steps.title: The elders of the family slept on the stone ledges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the זקני בית אב slept there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The elders of the family group slept there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: the older כהנים of the family on duty slept there, on the stone ledges just described. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each family group (בית אב) served in the בית המקדש on its own day. The older כהנים of that group had the honor of sleeping on the raised stone ledges (the רובדין from the last steps), not on the floor.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of the family group of כהנים serving that day
A family group of כהנים; each one served on a set day of the week

phrases.english: The elders of the family group sleep there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה after finishing the discussion of the רובדין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The elders of the family on duty slept on the stone ledges of the בית המוקד.

steps.title: Why not bring beds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the elders slept on hard stone instead of bringing in beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why sleep on stones? Let them bring in beds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: if the elders deserved comfort, why make them sleep on stone? They should just bring beds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes nothing stops them from bringing beds into the בית המוקד. Sleeping on hard stone ledges seems needlessly uncomfortable for the honored elders.

phrases.english: But why? Let them bring in beds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the arrangement described in the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's description of the elders sleeping on the stone ledges.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Beds would be more comfortable, so why not use them?

steps.title: Bringing beds into the בית המקדש is not respectful
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that it is not proper behavior to bring beds into the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not proper conduct to bring beds into the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question: beds do not belong in the בית המקדש, because it is not respectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not comfort but respect. Beds are ordinary household furniture, and bringing them into the holy place would treat it like a home. So the elders used the built-in stone ledges instead.
steps.whatToRemember: The elders slept on stone ledges, not beds, because bringing beds into the בית המקדש is not respectful.

phrases.english: אביי said:
It is not proper conduct
to bring beds into the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a reason the obvious solution cannot be used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beds could simply be brought in for comfort.
steps.terutzMaskana: Beds are not brought into the בית המקדש out of respect.

steps.title: The young כהנים slept on the floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the young כהנים slept with their garments on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: The young כהנים: each one slept with his garment on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה: the young כהנים did not get the stone ledges, and each slept on the floor on his own garment. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see the contrast: the elders slept on the raised ledges, and the young כהנים slept on the floor, using their own clothing to lie on.

keyTerms.meaning: Young כהנים, literally "blossoms of the priesthood"

phrases.english: The young men of the priesthood, each man with his garment on the ground.
phrases.notes: The word 'slept' is carried over from the line before: each one slept on his garment spread on the floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה after the discussion of the elders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The young כהנים slept on the floor, each on his own garment.

steps.title: Why are the young כהנים called by two different names?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why another משנה calls the young כהנים רובים while this one calls them by a different name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it that there the תנא calls them רובים, and here he calls them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the young כהנים have a different name in another משנה and starts to ask why the תנא changed the word. The question finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In another place the תנא calls the young כהנים רובים, but here he calls them פרחי כהונה. The גמרא wants to know why the wording changed, since both names seem to describe the same people.

keyTerms.meaning: Young men, the other name used for the young כהנים

phrases.english: Why is it that there he calls them "young men" (rovim),
phrases.notes: 'There' points to another משנה that describes these same young כהנים.

phrases.english: while here he calls them

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up on the term פרחי כהונה just quoted in step 20 and compares it with another משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנא uses two different names for the young כהנים in two places.
